messages:
Alex: Heads-up — seeing intermittent NXDOMAIN + SERVFAIL from edge workers when fetching modelpull.internal in ap-south-1. Started ~06:10 UTC. Affects prefetch and sporadic GPU provisioning failures. Anyone else?
Priya: Yep saw a spike in prefetch errors around the same time. Logs show repeated dig failures, then success after ~30s. No obvious pod restarts.
Marco: Could be NAT port exhaustion or a resolver path flip. Any pattern by AZ?
Alex: Mostly az-2 and az-3. az-1 looks fine.
Janice: Curious — our container image has /etc/resolv.conf pinned by the init hook, but systemd-resolved was rolled in last week on some hosts. Could be split-horizon where internal name resolves differently depending on which stub resolver you hit.
Priya: Dumping dig output from a failing node: 
```
$ dig +short modelpull.internal @127.0.0.53
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> +short modelpull.internal @127.0.0.53
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
$ dig +trace modelpull.internal
;; global options: +cmd
modelpull.internal. 60 IN CNAME modelpull.svc.cluster.local.
modelpull.svc.cluster.local. 60 IN A 10.240.5.12
```
It sometimes returns the A, sometimes NXDOMAIN from 127.0.0.53.
Marco: That smells like rrset reordering between the local stub and the upstream recursive. If the stub queries different forwarders in rotation (rotate option), responses might be inconsistent due to stale cache or split-horizon answers.
Janice: Check /etc/resolv.conf on the failing container host — we had 'options rotate' enabled for one of the utility images for load-testing. If rotate picks an external forwarder that doesn't know about internal zones, you'll get NXDOMAIN.
Alex: Here's /etc/resolv.conf from a failing host: 
```
nameserver 127.0.0.53
nameserver 10.10.1.5
search infra.example.internal svc.cluster.local
options single-request rotate timeout:1 ndots:5
```
Note: second nameserver is an edge recursive that should know internal zones, but sometimes the stub resolver hits 127.0.0.53 which forwards to an upstream pool that doesn't.
Priya: Also seeing negative TTLs being cached for modelpull.internal on the edge recursive (cache hit of NXDOMAIN with TTL 300). That explains the 30-60s flapping.
Alex: ops-bot created INC-2026-042 for tracking :white_check_mark:
SRE-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 created — priority P2. Assigned to eng-infra.
Marco: Quick mitigation: disable 'rotate' and force single best recursive on the stub (or reorder resolv.conf to prefer internal resolver). Also consider lowering negative-cache TTL for internal zones.
Janice: We pushed a DaemonSet that updates /etc/resolv.conf inside the test pool to remove 'rotate' and set 'options timeout:2 ndots:2'. Rolling now to az-2 first.
Priya: After removing rotate, prefetch errors dropped immediately in az-2. az-3 still has ~10% failures, looks like a subset of hosts still pointing to old resolv.conf.
Alex: Can we also add health-checking on the recursive pool so we avoid routing queries to forwarders that return NXDOMAIN for internal suffixes? Maybe tag forwarders with 'internal-aware' boolean and prefer them via local policy.
Marco: Agree. Long-term: enforce consistent split-horizon forwarding at the node level (don't let systemd-resolved or CNI mutate resolver order unpredictably). Also add telemetry: per-node resolver upstream used + NXDOMAIN rate.
Janice: Filed follow-up RFC for resolver orchestration and negative-ttl controls. Draft link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/resolver-orchestration (WIP).
Alex: Thanks all — keeping INC open until last_message_ts with full remediation notes.
Priya: Note for postmortem: mention containerd/hook ordering bug that allowed rotate to slip into some hosts during image refresh. That's the root cause for the uneven AZ distribution. :memo:
Marco: Closing loop — applied negative-ttl override to edge recursive for *.internal to 10s; will monitor for regressions.
ops-bot: Deployed DaemonSet resolver-fix to 42 hosts in az-2/az-3.
Alex: Confirmed: GPU provisioning errors back to baseline. Will post a short postmortem tomorrow. :+1:
